Context/Background: In a prospective endometrial carcinoma (EC) cohort, we performed a differential analysis of protein levels between hotspot-mutated CTNNB1 and WT CTNNB1 tumors, in the CNV-L subgroup.  In a separate analysis, we found that CTNNB1 S45 phosphorylation was significantly downregulated in hotspot-mutated tumors, whereas phosphosites distant from the hotspot mutations were mostly upregulated.
Prompt: Provide a discussion of the results from the differential analysis and any relevance to the mutation state of CTNNB1.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
We analyzed quantitative proteomics data comparing CTNNB1‐hotspot–mutant versus wild‐type (WT) endometrial carcinomas within the CNV‐low molecular subgroup.  Proteins were quantified and tested for differential abundance (n = 10 150 proteins; L2FC, T‐score, P‐value, FDR).  CTNNB1 itself (L2FC = 0.76, FDR ~ 1.7×10⁻¹¹) and known Wnt pathway effectors (e.g., AXIN1, LEF1, DKK4, LRP4) were among the most significantly upregulated proteins in CTNNB1‐mutant tumors.  CTNNB1 S45 phosphorylation was separately found to be downregulated in hotspot mutants (not quantified in this dataset).  Tissue: endometrial carcinoma; assay: proteomic differential analysis; contrast: CTNNB1 hotspot vs WT.

Keywords  
• CTNNB1 mutation  
• Wnt/β-catenin signaling  
• Endometrial carcinoma  
• Protein abundance  

Candidate Genes  
CTNNB1, AXIN1, LEF1, LRP4, DKK4  

Pathway Enrichments  
Enrichment of upregulated proteins (n = 778) highlighted strong over‐representation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling.  No downregulated pathway met equivalent significance.

| Theme                                    | Direction | Leading Genes                  |
|------------------------------------------|-----------|--------------------------------|
| HALLMARK_WNT_BETA_CATENIN_SIGNALING      | Up        | CTNNB1, AXIN1, LEF1, LRP4      |

Discussion  
Upregulated CTNNB1 and its core regulators (AXIN1, LEF1, LRP4) indicate activation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling in CTNNB1‐hotspot tumors.  Over 40% of significant proteins were increased in mutants, with canonical Wnt targets among the most enriched.  This suggests that exon‐3 CTNNB1 mutations drive broad Wnt pathway upregulation at the protein level, consistent with loss of β-catenin degradation.  Downregulated phosphorylation at S45 likely reflects altered access to kinases (e.g., CK1α), reinforcing constitutive β-catenin activation.  Therapeutically, Wnt pathway inhibitors or modulators of CTNNB1 phosphorylation may merit investigation in CTNNB1‐mutant endometrial carcinoma.

Targeted (Keyword‐Guided) Subset  
Filtering enrichment for “WNT” yielded GO_WNT_SIGNALING_PATHWAY and multiple Hallmark WNT gene sets among the top hits, all driven by the same leading proteins (CTNNB1, AXIN1, LEF1, LRP4).

Key Genes/Proteins (Leading Edge)  
Upregulated Wnt effectors:

| Gene    | Direction | Role/Function                               | Pathway(s)               |
|---------|-----------|---------------------------------------------|--------------------------|
| CTNNB1  | Up        | β-Catenin; adherens junction, Wnt TF co-factor | Wnt/β-catenin signaling  |
| AXIN1   | Up        | Scaffold for β-catenin destruction complex    | Wnt/β-catenin signaling  |
| LEF1    | Up        | Transcription factor for Wnt target genes    | Wnt/β-catenin signaling  |
| LRP4    | Up        | Wnt co-receptor modulator                    | Wnt/β-catenin signaling  |
| DKK4    | Up        | Secreted Wnt inhibitor                       | Wnt/β-catenin signaling  |

Downregulated Wnt regulators: not observed in this dataset.

Comparisons  
Findings are specific to proteomic data in CNV-low endometrial carcinoma and align with known CTNNB1 hotspot effects.  No discordant tissue‐specific signals were observed.

Implications  
CTNNB1 exon‐3 mutations promote upregulation of Wnt pathway proteins, likely via impaired S45 phosphorylation and increased β-catenin stability.  Targeting β-catenin–TCF interactions or restoring S45 phosphorylation may offer therapeutic avenues in CTNNB1-mutant tumors.

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate Wnt activation at the single‐cell level in CTNNB1‐mutant EC via phospho‐β-catenin (S45) immunohistochemistry.  
2. Test Wnt pathway inhibitors (e.g., tankyrase or porcupine inhibitors) in CTNNB1-mutant versus WT EC cell models.  
3. Quantify CTNNB1 S45 and other phosphosite levels in the same cohort to correlate phosphorylation loss with protein‐level Wnt activation.  
4. Assess downstream transcriptional changes in canonical Wnt targets by RNA‐seq in CTNNB1-mutant tumors.

Introduction/Context  
We analyzed quantitative proteomics data comparing CTNNB1‐hotspot–mutant versus wild‐type (WT) endometrial carcinomas within the CNV‐low molecular subgroup.  Proteins were quantified and tested for differential abundance (n = 10 150 proteins; L2FC, T‐score, P‐value, FDR).  CTNNB1 itself (L2FC = 0.76, FDR ~ 1.7×10⁻¹¹) and known Wnt pathway effectors (e.g., AXIN1, LEF1, DKK4, LRP4) were among the most significantly upregulated proteins in CTNNB1‐mutant tumors.  CTNNB1 S45 phosphorylation was separately found to be downregulated in hotspot mutants (not quantified in this dataset).  Tissue: endometrial carcinoma; assay: proteomic differential analysis; contrast: CTNNB1 hotspot vs WT.

Keywords  
• CTNNB1 mutation  
• Wnt/β-catenin signaling  
• Endometrial carcinoma  
• Protein abundance  

Candidate Genes  
CTNNB1, AXIN1, LEF1, LRP4, DKK4  

Pathway Enrichments  
Enrichment of upregulated proteins (n = 778) highlighted strong over‐representation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling.  No downregulated pathway met equivalent significance.

| Theme                                    | Direction | Leading Genes                  |
|------------------------------------------|-----------|--------------------------------|
| HALLMARK_WNT_BETA_CATENIN_SIGNALING      | Up        | CTNNB1, AXIN1, LEF1, LRP4      |

Discussion  
Upregulated CTNNB1 and its core regulators (AXIN1, LEF1, LRP4) indicate activation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling in CTNNB1‐hotspot tumors.  Over 40% of significant proteins were increased in mutants, with canonical Wnt targets among the most enriched.  This suggests that exon‐3 CTNNB1 mutations drive broad Wnt pathway upregulation at the protein level, consistent with loss of β-catenin degradation.  Downregulated phosphorylation at S45 likely reflects altered access to kinases (e.g., CK1α), reinforcing constitutive β-catenin activation.  Therapeutically, Wnt pathway inhibitors or modulators of CTNNB1 phosphorylation may merit investigation in CTNNB1‐mutant endometrial carcinoma.

Targeted (Keyword‐Guided) Subset  
Filtering enrichment for “WNT” yielded GO_WNT_SIGNALING_PATHWAY and multiple Hallmark WNT gene sets among the top hits, all driven by the same leading proteins (CTNNB1, AXIN1, LEF1, LRP4).

Key Genes/Proteins (Leading Edge)  
Upregulated Wnt effectors:

| Gene    | Direction | Role/Function                               | Pathway(s)               |
|---------|-----------|---------------------------------------------|--------------------------|
| CTNNB1  | Up        | β-Catenin; adherens junction, Wnt TF co-factor | Wnt/β-catenin signaling  |
| AXIN1   | Up        | Scaffold for β-catenin destruction complex    | Wnt/β-catenin signaling  |
| LEF1    | Up        | Transcription factor for Wnt target genes    | Wnt/β-catenin signaling  |
| LRP4    | Up        | Wnt co-receptor modulator                    | Wnt/β-catenin signaling  |
| DKK4    | Up        | Secreted Wnt inhibitor                       | Wnt/β-catenin signaling  |

Downregulated Wnt regulators: not observed in this dataset.

Comparisons  
Findings are specific to proteomic data in CNV-low endometrial carcinoma and align with known CTNNB1 hotspot effects.  No discordant tissue‐specific signals were observed.

Implications  
CTNNB1 exon‐3 mutations promote upregulation of Wnt pathway proteins, likely via impaired S45 phosphorylation and increased β-catenin stability.  Targeting β-catenin–TCF interactions or restoring S45 phosphorylation may offer therapeutic avenues in CTNNB1-mutant tumors.

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate Wnt activation at the single‐cell level in CTNNB1‐mutant EC via phospho‐β-catenin (S45) immunohistochemistry.  
2. Test Wnt pathway inhibitors (e.g., tankyrase or porcupine inhibitors) in CTNNB1-mutant versus WT EC cell models.  
3. Quantify CTNNB1 S45 and other phosphosite levels in the same cohort to correlate phosphorylation loss with protein‐level Wnt activation.  
4. Assess downstream transcriptional changes in canonical Wnt targets by RNA‐seq in CTNNB1-mutant tumors.
